stories.headline: Final Times/Siena polls show Democrats ahead in five of seven key Senate races on the eve of the midterms
stories.summary: The last New York Times/Siena polls of likely voters (taken Oct 23–Nov 1) show Democrats leading in Michigan (El-Sayed 53%, Rogers 42%), Texas (Talarico 50%, Paxton 43%), Maine (Jackson 51%, Collins 45%), Ohio (Brown 49%, Husted 44%) and Kansas (Hamilton 49%, Marshall 44%). Alaska (Peltola 48%, Sullivan 46%) and Iowa (Turek 48%, Hinson 47%) are within the margin of error. Siena's director said a Democratic Senate majority is 'a distinct possibility' but either party could still win it. CBS News, citing the University of Florida Voting Lab, says more than 54 million Americans had already voted early.
stories.why: Republicans hold the Senate 53-47; CNN notes that winning the four GOP-held seats where Democrats lead outside the margin of error, while holding their own seats, would flip control. Polls are not results.
stories.label: Reported
stories.note: Polls are snapshots with margins of error of roughly ±3.4 to ±5 points per state; most fieldwork ended before Haley Stevens endorsed Mike Rogers on Nov 1.

stories.headline: Stevens won't explain her switch to backing Republican Rogers; El-Sayed says he raised $1.2M+ since
stories.summary: In her first interview since endorsing GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers, Rep. Haley Stevens told CNN's Anderson Cooper her endorsement is 'rock solid' and that 'nothing with me changed', but did not say what changed her mind after she reportedly told Rep. Debbie Dingell on Saturday night she would not endorse him. She again cited El-Sayed's ties to streamer Hasan Piker and an outside group's ad tying grocery costs to the war in Gaza, which El-Sayed's campaign says it had nothing to do with. Her chief of staff said most of her congressional staff resigned. El-Sayed's campaign told CBS it raised more than $1.2 million after the endorsement.
stories.why: Michigan's open seat is one of the races that decides Senate control; the final Times/Siena poll there (mostly taken before the switch) had El-Sayed up 11.
stories.label: Reported
stories.note: Ongoing: the endorsement itself led the Nov 1 Evening Edition.

stories.headline: Trump set to close the campaign at the Reflecting Pool; says he'll be 'Mr. Veto' if Democrats win Congress
stories.summary: President Trump was scheduled to hold telerallies and an afternoon event Monday at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, whose troubled renovation he has championed; as of this morning's edition the event had not yet taken place. He finished his in-person rallies Sunday in Iowa and Kansas. In a New York Post podcast taped Friday and released Monday, he said that if Republicans lose, 'I veto everything' until Democrats come to make deals. CBS notes the Justice Department has acknowledged in court that a contractor's 'botched installation', not vandals as Trump claimed, caused the pool's peeling paint.
stories.why: Trump's planned closing message frames Tuesday as a vote on his agenda; a Democratic Congress would mean divided government for his last two years.

stories.headline: All nine aboard killed as a Learjet nose-dives onto a road in Palm Beach County, Florida
stories.summary: A Learjet 60 flying from Austin, Texas, to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas crashed onto Military Trail near Cresthaven around 12:50 p.m. ET Sunday, killing all nine people on board, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. Air-traffic audio has a crew member reporting ice, turbulence and precipitation, then a descent of 20,000 feet per minute. Gov. Ron DeSantis said no one on the ground was reported hurt; about 600 residents of a nearby mobile-home park were evacuated and officials say the road will be closed for at least 30 days. The victims have not been named; the NTSB and FAA are investigating.
stories.why: The victims and the cause, including the role of bad weather, are not yet known; the NTSB investigation will take months.
stories.label: Reported

stories.headline: Formal Canada-U.S. trade talks expected to resume within days; Trump says the two sides have 'the concept of a very good deal'
stories.summary: After a Saturday call Prime Minister Mark Carney called a 'good conversation', a source told The Globe and Mail that Trump ordered his team to resume formal talks, with negotiations expected to start in a few days and pick up where they stalled, including on autos. Speaking in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said the countries were 'very close' and had 'the concept of a deal' that would be 'great for our farmers' and 'fine for Canada too'. Canada walked away from the table in August.
stories.why: Tariffs have hit Canadian autos, steel and other exports; a restart could shape Thursday's federal budget and the wider economy.
stories.label: Reported + unnamed sources
stories.note: Ongoing: the Carney-Trump call was in the Nov 1 Evening Edition. The talks restart comes from one unnamed source; no date has been announced.

stories.headline: Western Canada didn't fall back: B.C., Alberta, Manitoba, northwestern Ontario and N.W.T. stay on daylight time
stories.summary: Clocks did not change on Sunday across British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, northwestern Ontario and the Northwest Territories, which chose year-round daylight time. Mornings will be darker: by late December the sun won't rise until about 9:30 a.m. in Winnipeg and 9:50 a.m. in Edmonton. The Canada Border Services Agency shifted hours at 26 land crossings to match U.S. states, Lloydminster no longer has to juggle two times, and schools and ski hills are adjusting; airlines and phone carriers say operations are normal.
stories.why: Much of Canada is now on a different clock relationship with the U.S. and the rest of the country, which matters for travel, cross-border business and scheduling.
stories.label: Reported

stories.headline: Carney heads to Antigua for the Commonwealth summit as its chief pitches the bloc as an alternative to U.S. trade
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney leaves Monday for his first Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in St. John's, Antigua and Barbuda, where King Charles presides over ceremonies on Tuesday. Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey told CBC that all 56 members 'had been slapped with tariffs' and that intra-Commonwealth trade, about $900 billion, should more than double. Canadian officials say Canada does about $100 billion a year in trade with Commonwealth partners. Carney is expected back in Ottawa after Tuesday to prepare Thursday's federal budget.
stories.why: It is part of Carney's push to diversify trade away from the U.S., and it overlaps with U.S. Election Day.

stories.headline: Ontario drops its minimum sleeping-space rule for jails; civil liberties groups want it back
stories.summary: Ontario amended its Building Code last month to remove a requirement of at least 4.7 square metres of sleeping area per person in provincial adult jails. The Solicitor General's office says the change aligns with the National Building Code and helps add more than 2,500 permanent jail spaces; it says the old rule blocked adding a top bunk to an eight-square-metre cell. The Canadian Civil Liberties Association and Elizabeth Fry Societies say it was made without consultation and will normalize double and triple bunking, with northern jails such as Thunder Bay's hit hardest.
stories.why: Most people in Ontario's provincial jails are awaiting trial, and courts have criticized overcrowding there.
stories.label: Reported + opinion

Wong said AI will be used to flag anomalies in documents, but people will make final decisions.

stories.headline: About 600,000 visitors over the Halloween weekend, up 34%, with record crossings at Huanggang
stories.summary: Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki said about 600,000 visitors arrived Friday through Sunday, about 470,000 from the mainland and 130,000 from elsewhere, up 34% from a year earlier. More than 150,000 people a day crossed at the Lok Ma Chau–Huanggang control point on both Saturday and Sunday, a record, and more than 20,000 left through it between midnight and 2 a.m. on Nov 1. He said bar takings were up 30–50% over the past two weekends and the Wine & Dine Festival drew 171,000 visits.
stories.why: Tourism and spending are key to Hong Kong's recovery, and the crowds test cross-border transport.

stories.headline: HKMA pilot lets its 12 participating banks settle tokenised deposits 24/7 in tokenised central-bank money
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority said EnsembleTX, the controlled pilot phase of its Project Ensemble, now supports 24/7 interbank settlement of tokenised-deposit transactions in tokenised central bank money for participating banks. Since its launch in November 2025 the pilot had settled these transactions through the HKD Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system; the HKMA says the new capability allows settlement beyond conventional operating hours. Participation grew to 12 banks, including HSBC, Standard Chartered and Bank of China (Hong Kong), and 20 'industry pioneer' firms such as BlackRock and Ant International. The SFC's chief executive said it enables round-the-clock corporate treasury and tokenised-fund trading. It remains a controlled pilot for participating banks and firms, not a general service.
stories.why: It is a step toward money moving outside banking hours, part of Hong Kong's bid to lead in tokenised finance during FinTech Week, though for now only within the pilot.
stories.label: Official statement

stories.headline: China's central bank switches its main policy rate to an overnight rate at 1.25%
stories.summary: The People's Bank of China injected 541 billion yuan through overnight reverse repos at 1.25% on Monday, the first operation under a new framework that makes the overnight rate its main policy rate instead of the seven-day rate. It will run overnight operations every working day. Analysts quoted by Reuters said it works like a targeted 15-basis-point cut for financial institutions, though Citi called it a 'mark-to-market adjustment' and does not expect a loan prime rate cut in November.
stories.why: It changes how China signals borrowing costs, and it comes as credit worries at state developer Zhuhai Huafa have rattled bond markets.
stories.label: Reported + analysis

stories.headline: Oman's sultan makes first-ever state visit to China; joint statement urges U.S.-Iran talks and reopening Hormuz
stories.summary: Sultan Haitham bin Tarik held talks with Xi Jinping in Beijing on Monday, the first visit by an Omani sultan in 48 years of diplomatic ties. The two sides signed a currency-swap agreement, 14 memorandums (including AI, BeiDou navigation, space and digital currency) and a protocol on date exports. Their joint statement called on the U.S. and Iran to reach a comprehensive ceasefire, return to the 'Islamabad memorandum' and restore safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.why: China is Oman's biggest trading partner, and Oman is a key mediator in the Iran war that is choking Gulf oil shipping.

stories.headline: Iran says it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the U.S. meets its conditions
stories.summary: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday the two-day timeline, down from seven days proposed in September, shows 'good faith', but 'everything depends' on Washington. Iran's conditions include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. naval blockade; Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi added more demands. A deputy foreign minister went to Doha to help draft a preliminary agreement with Qatar mediating. Trump has said there will be no new strikes before the U.S. vote but has not ruled them out afterward. No deal has been announced.
stories.why: Hormuz carries a large share of the world's oil and gas; its closure has pushed up fuel and energy prices worldwide.
stories.label: Reported + claim
stories.note: Ongoing: the Qatar-mediated talks were in Edition 1 (Nov 1). Iran's offer is conditional and unverified.

stories.headline: Binance reopens withdrawals after a $6B+ hack the FBI blames on North Korea; $3.6B net outflow on day one
stories.summary: The world's largest crypto exchange resumed withdrawals in phases on Sunday after more than $6 billion in assets were stolen around Oct. 29, thought to be the biggest crypto theft ever. The FBI said North Korea's 'TraderTraitor' group was responsible; Trump said 'we don't know if it's North Korea'. Binance said it processed $4.65 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits Sunday, a $3.64 billion net outflow (about 2.1% of assets), and that it has replenished 90% of the stolen tokens with company funds and will cover the rest.
stories.why: A run on the biggest exchange tests confidence in crypto markets, and the theft would be a major source of money for sanctioned North Korea.
stories.label: Reported + allegation
stories.note: North Korea's role is the FBI's attribution, not a court finding.

stories.headline: Belgian PM Bart De Wever offers his resignation after budget talks collapse; the king holds off
stories.summary: De Wever went to the palace Monday after his five-party 'Arizona' coalition failed overnight to agree how to find about €10 billion in savings for 2027. King Philippe took the resignation 'under consideration', will consult coalition party leaders from Tuesday and meets De Wever again Friday, urging compromise. The split is left-right: Vooruit, CD&V and Les Engagés want more from higher earners; N-VA and MR want spending cuts. Belgium's deficit was 5% of GDP last year, above the EU's 3% limit.
stories.why: A government collapse could mean emergency monthly budgets or new elections in a country that hosts the EU and NATO.
stories.label: Reported
stories.note: What happens if the king accepts is unclear: Euronews says new elections would follow; VRT says a new majority could in principle be formed without them.

stories.headline: Russia resumes strikes on Kherson after the war's longest truce ends; alert apps hacked on both sides
stories.summary: A local ceasefire in Ukraine's Kherson region that let hundreds of people leave Russian-occupied Oleshky ended Sunday night; a Ukrainian official told AFP Russia refused to extend it. On Monday morning a Russian drone hit a car in Kherson's Korabelny district, wounding two older residents, local authorities said. Ukraine's air-alert app sent fake radiation warnings Sunday night, and Russia said its emergency-warning app suffered a 'massive cyberattack' on Monday. US-mediated talks are due to resume this month.
stories.why: The truce was the only real pause in fighting in the full-scale war; its end leaves civilians exposed again as winter power cuts deepen.
stories.label: Reported + allegation
stories.note: Ongoing: the Oleshky evacuations were in Edition 1 (Nov 1). Claims about who attacked the apps are unverified.

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli, 20, becomes F1's youngest world champion as Verstappen wins in Mexico City
stories.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli clinched the 2026 title by finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix, at 20 years and 68 days, breaking Sebastian Vettel's record (23 in 2010). He is the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. Max Verstappen won from fifth on the grid, holding off Lewis Hamilton by 0.8 seconds in a race with a red flag after Valtteri Bottas crashed (he got out unaided) and a late safety car. The season continues in São Paulo on Nov. 6–8.
stories.why: It is a new age record for the sport and Italy's first drivers' title in 73 years, with races still to run.

stories.headline: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers for Senate, two days before the vote
stories.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, appeared with GOP nominee Mike Rogers at a Detroit church on Sunday and then endorsed him in a video. She said El-Sayed had told her she was no longer welcome at his events. She has criticized him over his past campaigning with streamer Hasan Piker and over an ad by Cenk Uygur blaming Israel for high grocery prices; El-Sayed's campaign says it had nothing to do with the ad and criticized it. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called the move a "despicable betrayal"; El-Sayed told reporters it doesn't matter to voters. Trump praised her at his Iowa rally.
stories.why: Michigan's open seat is one of the races that decides whether Democrats can win the Senate, and the split exposes a wider Democratic rift over Israel.

stories.headline: Judge throws out DOJ bid to set aside 'second Dan Sullivan' ballots in Alaska; DOJ appeals
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason on Sunday dismissed the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to separate ballots cast for little-known candidate Daniel J. Sullivan and to hold off certifying the Senate race if Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan loses. She wrote that the request would violate Alaskans' right to a secret ballot. The department said it will appeal. Republicans allege Democrat Mary Peltola's camp recruited the second Sullivan to confuse voters; Peltola denies it. Separately, California Gov. Gavin Newsom on Oct 31 wrote to the state's four chief federal judges warning they may be asked for warrants to seize ballots before results are certified.
stories.why: Courts are now refereeing how votes are counted and certified in races that could decide control of Congress.
stories.label: Fact + allegation

stories.headline: NYC voters: five city charter questions are on the back of Tuesday's ballot
stories.summary: Besides the races for Congress and state offices, New York City ballots carry five yes-or-no charter amendments from the Commission on Government Efficiency (COGE), the 2026 charter review commission: (1) faster permits for sidewalk cafes, ramps and planters; (2) less contractor paperwork; (3) quicker street-safety projects, sales of unused city property and office leasing, with City Planning Commission approval instead of a Council vote on property sales; (4) a central construction-permit hub at the Buildings Department; and (5) a target for the city's rainy-day reserves. Polls are open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Nov 3.
stories.why: Question 3 in particular would shift some land-sale decisions away from the City Council, so it's worth reading before you vote.

stories.headline: Alberta's elections chief says: keep the old riding map or delay the 2027 vote
stories.summary: In a letter dated Oct 30, Chief Electoral Officer Gordon McClure told MLAs that Elections Alberta needs 12 to 18 months to run an election on new boundaries and cannot prepare for two maps at once, so the Oct 18, 2027 election should use current boundaries or be postponed. A contested boundary report is due in the legislature Monday. NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi says the proposed map gerrymanders Calgary and Lethbridge and vows a court challenge; Premier Danielle Smith denies manipulating the vote. The justice minister's office says it is reviewing the letter.
stories.why: It raises the prospect of Alberta's next election being delayed amid a fight over fair representation.

stories.headline: Ottawa quietly shelves the 'Jane Goodall Act' on elephant and great ape captivity
stories.summary: The bill, which would have banned new captivity, breeding and import or export of elephants and great apes except for conservation, welfare or research, passed the Senate in 2024 but died when Parliament was prorogued in January 2025. Despite a 2025 Liberal campaign pledge, the environment minister's office told CBC no decision has been made to reintroduce it. Advocates suspect the government's focus on the tariff war. About 23 elephants live in Canada.
stories.why: Ottawa says zoos and animal welfare are mainly provincial matters, so for now there's no national rule on keeping these animals.

stories.headline: Rioting and looting in Frankfurt after Germany's 'Gen Z' protests; 100+ police hurt

In Frankfurt, rioters later damaged 17 shops and looted five, attacking police with stones, fireworks and petrol bombs. Police arrested 54 people aged 13 to 29; more than 100 officers were injured. Hesse's interior minister said most suspects were German nationals but many had immigrant backgrounds; the city's mayor said passports don't matter, only accountability. stories.headline: Shenzhen tightens security and bans drones ahead of APEC summit
stories.summary: Guangdong police are stepping up security, including drone bans, before the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, where Xi and Trump are expected to meet. stories.why: The summit is the next big moment for the US-China trade truce.

stories.summary: State broadcaster CGTN reports the year's box office, including presales, has topped 31.5 billion yuan, and highlights a push to pair films with sports events to drive spending.

stories.headline: Iran holds talks via Qatar as region braces for possible US strikes after the midterms
stories.summary: Iranian envoys met Qatari mediators in Doha on Saturday on ways to end the Gulf war, Reuters reported, citing a source. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump hasn't decided on new strikes and prefers diplomacy. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered the armed forces to respond immediately and without geographic limits to any attack.
stories.why: A return to fighting could hit oil prices and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.label: Fact + analysis
stories.note: Talks details come from one anonymous source.

stories.headline: Canelo Alvarez regains WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh
stories.summary: Mexico's Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez, 36, beat France's previously unbeaten Christian Mbilli by unanimous decision (115-112, 116-111, 117-110) in his first fight since losing to Terence Crawford in September 2025. AFP notes the bout went ahead despite Houthi drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia that have called off other events.
stories.why: Boxing's biggest star is back as a champion, and the fight shows Saudi Arabia keeping big events going despite the conflict.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Spain's deadliest high-speed rail crash kills 69; probe focuses on control center
stories.summary: A Renfe high-speed train slammed into a stopped Iryo train near Urda, south of Madrid, on Wednesday, killing at least 69 people. Investigators are looking at how the control center responded after a safety signaling system failed on the Madrid-Seville line.
stories.why: It raises questions about safety on one of Europe's busiest high-speed networks.
stories.label: Fact
stories.note: Cause is still under investigation.

stories.headline: Oleshky civilians reach Ukraine under a rare truce as Russian strikes cut power
stories.summary: Exhausted residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky crossed into Ukraine under a six-day local ceasefire mediated by US first lady Melania Trump with the Pope's involvement, after a long trip via Crimea, Russia and Belarus. Meanwhile, Russian strikes left tens of thousands without power, including in Kyiv.
stories.why: It is the first humanitarian truce of its kind in more than four years of war.
stories.label: Fact

stories.headline: Mayon volcano erupts in the Philippines; 2,000+ evacuated
stories.summary: A moderately explosive eruption on Oct 30 sent ash 3 km high and put Mayon on Alert Level 3. More than 2,000 people were evacuated, and about 420 families spent All Saints' Day in evacuation centers.
stories.why: Mayon is the Philippines' most active volcano, and a bigger eruption would force more evacuations.
stories.label: Fact
